evals.prompt: Our FreeCAD robot wrist has two configurations and 146 linked occurrences. Create a production BOM contract that reconciles the CAD eBOM to an mBOM, includes adhesives, cable labels and packaging, controls servo and bearing alternates by serial effectivity, and reports where-used impact for a bearing revision change.
evals.expected_output: A lifecycle BOM contract and review that preserve occurrence identity, map eBOM to mBOM, govern alternates/effectivity, include non-geometric items, and provide where-used/change evidence without claiming ERP or physical verification.
assertions: Distinguishes eBOM, mBOM, as-built, and as-maintained states
Includes structured effectivity and approved alternate controls
Reconciles CAD and non-geometric BOM content in both directions
Reports transitive where-used and manufacturing/service change impact

evals.prompt: Build the as-built genealogy and software manifest for 20 mobile robots. Each has serialized motors, lot-controlled batteries, unit-specific encoder substitutions under deviation, and controller firmware plus calibration hashes. Include the acceptance gates and validator workflow.
evals.expected_output: A serial/lot genealogy and firmware baseline with deviation scope, evidence, immutable maintenance transitions, and honest validation boundaries.
assertions: Tracks product, occurrence, part revision, serial, and lot relationships
Scopes substitutions to approved units rather than global alternates
Captures firmware version, target, checksum, calibration, and evidence
Does not claim the validator proves the physical build

evals.prompt: Roll up cost and supply risk for an aluminum actuator assembly at quantities 10, 100 and 1000. Purchased electronics have price breaks, one MCU is single-source and near end-of-life, machining cost comes from a separate manufacturing plan, and some quotes have expired. Prevent phantom and embedded-cost double counting.
evals.expected_output: A normalized cost and sourcing analysis with quantity/basis provenance, missing/expired-cost flags, supply risks, approved-source coverage, and double-count prevention.
assertions: Normalizes currency, date, quantity break, batch size, and cost type
Imports rather than reinvents manufacturing conversion cost
Flags uncosted, expired, single-source, and lifecycle risks
Avoids double counting phantom groups and embedded purchased-assembly cost
